citeAs: Talmor, A., Herzig, J., Lourie, N., and Berant, J. (2019). CommonsenseQA: A Question Answering Challenge Targeting Commonsense Knowledge. NAACL 2019.
creator: Alon Talmor, Jonathan Herzig, Nicholas Lourie, Jonathan Berant (Tel-Aviv University, Allen Institute for Artificial Intelligence)
description: CommonsenseQA is a challenging multiple-choice question answering dataset targeting commonsense knowledge. It contains 12,247 questions generated by crowd workers based on subgraphs from ConceptNet, where each question requires prior world knowledge to discriminate between semantically similar answer concepts. Each question is accompanied by five candidate answers (one correct, four distractors).
name: CommonsenseQA
publisher: Tel-Aviv University / Allen Institute for Artificial Intelligence
rai:annotationsPerItem: Each question was verified by 2 workers during the quality verification step.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Questions were verified by 2 workers each; only questions where at least one verifier answered correctly were retained. This filtering process removed 15% of the questions (from 16,242 formulated to 12,247 final examples). Human accuracy on a sample of 100 questions was measured at 88.9% (majority vote of 5 workers).
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: AMT workers were shown a question concept and three answer concepts from ConceptNet and asked to formulate three questions (one per target concept), ensuring each question has exactly one correct answer among the three targets. Workers were instructed to avoid using words strongly related to the answer concept (e.g., not using 'open' when the answer is 'door'). Workers also added two distractors per question: one chosen from ConceptNet concepts with the same relation, and one authored manually. A separate disjoint group of workers verified question quality by annotating each question as unanswerable or selecting the correct answer; questions verified correctly by at least one of two verifiers were retained. Only annotators with at least 75% question pass rate were accepted.
rai:dataBiases: Questions were generated from ConceptNet subgraphs, which may introduce biases from the knowledge base itself. The paper notes that 10 workers formulated more than 85% of the questions, suggesting potential annotator bias. The dataset was designed to avoid simple surface clues by instructing workers not to use words strongly related to the answer concept. The paper also notes that annotation artifacts (distributional biases) are a known challenge in commonsense datasets, and the use of semantically similar distractors (from the same ConceptNet relation) was specifically designed to reduce the ability of models to exploit surface-level cues.
rai:dataCollection: Questions were generated by Amazon Mechanical Turk (AMT) crowd workers. Workers were shown a source concept and three target concepts sampled from ConceptNet subgraphs, and asked to author three multiple-choice questions (one per target concept). Workers also added two additional distractors per question (one selected from ConceptNet, one authored manually). A separate group of workers verified question quality. Web snippets from Google Search were also collected for each question-answer pair to provide textual context.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: ConceptNet knowledge base (version 5.5), containing 32 million triplets of concepts connected by commonsense relations. A filtered subset of 236,208 triplets was used, organized into approximately 130,000 triplets (43,000 question sets) for crowdsourcing. Web snippets retrieved via Google Search were also used as raw context data.
rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Web Scraping, Secondary Data analysis
rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is grounded in ConceptNet, which may limit the diversity of commonsense phenomena covered. A small number of workers (10) formulated more than 85% of the questions, potentially limiting linguistic diversity. The best model (BERT-large) achieves only 55.9% accuracy, well below human performance (88.9%), indicating the task remains very challenging for current models. The paper notes that using web snippets as context does not substantially help models, suggesting the questions require deeper commonsense reasoning beyond surface retrieval.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The data was split into training/development/test sets with an 80/10/10 split. Two split strategies were used: (a) random split — questions split uniformly at random; (b) question concept split — each set has disjoint question concepts. The random split is considered the primary split. A SANITY mode was also defined where hard distractors are replaced with random ConceptNet distractors to verify baseline model behavior.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: ConceptNet triplets were filtered by: (1) removing general relations (e.g., RelatedTo) or well-explored NLP relations (e.g., IsA), retaining 22 relations; (2) removing triplets where a concept is more than four words or not in English; (3) removing triplets where the edit distance between source and target concepts is too low. This reduced 32 million triplets to 236,208 usable triplets. Questions failing the verification step (15%) were discarded.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is intended to advance research in commonsense reasoning for NLU systems. By providing a large-scale benchmark that is easy for humans but hard for machines, it highlights the gap between human and machine commonsense understanding, motivating future work in this area.
rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking commonsense question answering systems; evaluating the degree to which NLU models capture commonsense knowledge; facilitating research on incorporating commonsense knowledge into NLU systems.

null_reasons.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: No discussion of missing data handling in the collection process beyond the quality filtering step.
null_reasons.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: No specific timeframe or date range for data collection is mentioned in the paper.
null_reasons.rai:dataImputationProtocol: No imputation of missing values is described in the paper.
null_reasons.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: No versioning, update cadence, or maintenance plan is described in the paper.
null_reasons.rai:machineAnnotationTools: No ML models or automated tools were used in the annotation pipeline; ConceptNet was used as a knowledge source but not as an annotation tool.
